goals: Answer all 11 verification questions through implementation, testing, and documentation
Validate PiRunner's test specification lifecycle end-to-end
Verify artifact provenance, hash integrity, and event immutability

tasks.title: Implement and verify TestSpecification creation and acceptance (Q1)
Verify TestSuiteLock references the exact accepted TestSpecification artifact (Q3)
Compute and verify live hash equals the locked hash (Q4)
Verify authoritative execution uses the command from TestSpecification (Q5)
Verify TestExecutionResult references specification, hash, command, and repository revision (Q6)
Implement real Pi agent artifact emission and ingestion without synthetic provenance (Q7)
Test and verify unauthorized Pi tool call blocking (Q8)
Test workflow restart recovery to identical canonical state (Q9)
Test deliberate repository mutation producing conflict/HUMAN_GATE (Q10)
Verify PRESERVE append only adds evidence without modifying historical events (Q11)

acceptanceCriteria.statement: PiRunner successfully creates and accepts a TestSpecification artifact describing the current test suite
The accepted TestSpecification artifact contains a valid testSuiteContentHash field
The generated TestSuiteLock references the exact TestSpecification artifact ID
The computed live hash of the test suite matches the locked hash in TestSuiteLock
The authoritative test execution invokes the exact command specified in TestSpecification
TestExecutionResult artifact contains references to specification ID, hash, command, and repository revision
Real Pi agent emits artifacts that are successfully ingested without requiring synthetic provenance
Unauthorized real Pi tool calls are detected and blocked
Workflow restart recovers to the same canonical state with matching state hash
Deliberate repository mutation produces expected conflict detection and HUMAN_GATE state transition
PRESERVE operation appends new events without modifying historical event content or order
